verifiedAgainstRegulations.detail: The service publishes geography the authority's own current regulations say no longer exists. The 2026 summary states: "Deer management units 351 and 352 have been rescinded" and "The limited firearms deer zone has been eliminated." Both DMU-351 (Mideast Upper Peninsula) and DMU-352 (Midwest Upper Peninsula unit) are still returned by the layer, stamped Year='2026' like every other row and last edited 2026-09-22, and the LimitedFirearmZoneBoundary layer is still published. Verified live 2026-09-23. Michigan's map may therefore NOT be served as the service returns it: drawing 351 or 352 would show a hunter a rescinded unit as current, and no field on the layer distinguishes them — Year does not, because it says 2026 for all 115 rows.
verifiedAgainstRegulations.consequence: Parity against the authority's own GIS service is NOT sufficient certification here, because the service is the thing that is out of date. Michigan's map lane must be certified against the REGULATIONS as well as against the service, and the rescinded units excluded by an explicit, sourced exclusion list rather than by a rule inferred from the data.

geography.alsoUnreferenced: The 2026 summary does not mention DMU-333 (Lansing core CWD area), DMU-419 (Lansing CWD management zone), DMU-486 or DMU-487 (multicounty units) or DMU-499 (Urban deer management zone) at all, though it does sell a "DMU 487 antlerless deer license". Their legal basis is therefore in the Wildlife Conservation Order rather than the summary, and is unread. This is recorded as unread, not as absent.

WCO.pdf and every chapter PDF carry amendment history only through Am. 5 of 2026 (eff. 2026-04-08) and still contain the rescinded sections 3.124, 12.483 and 12.484 and the eliminated limited-firearms-zone definitions 1.2(17) and 2.1(4). precedence.evidence: Not merely unfound — absent by drafting choice, which is a stronger finding. Across 183 pages: 'precedence' 0 hits, 'supersede' 0, 'most restrictive' 0, 'shall govern' 0, 'shall control' 0, 'overlap' 0. The single 'more restrictive … shall prevail' concerns federal versus state migratory-bird permits, not geography. Where the drafters wanted mutual exclusion they wrote it into the definitions — §12.19b defines its unit as counties 'except those lands defined in section 12.33a' — so the absence elsewhere is deliberate. Units 486, 487, 499 and 333 genuinely overlap the county units and nothing resolves them: evaluate every containing unit and return CONFLICT.

servingDecision.kindNotDerivable: A unit's kind must be assigned per Chapter XII section and stored as data, never inferred. Decisive on its own: the layer contains code 261, which does not occur anywhere in the Wildlife Conservation Order. The GIS also contradicts the Order twice — DMU-499's GIS heading says 'Urban deer management zone' while §12.499's operative sentence defines a 'January archery deer management zone', and 359's number never appears in the body of its own section. Number ranges do not encode kind either (349/351, 354/359 and 486/487/499 are different kinds within the same hundreds).
servingDecision.unitsThatGovernNothing: DMU-486 governs nothing in the Order: the string 486 occurs only inside §12.486 itself. It is a licence-administration and mapping construct. DMU-487 by contrast is a row in §3.105a Table 4, which is why an antlerless licence for it is sellable.
servingDecision.lowerPeninsulaIsCounty: CONFIRMED from the Order's own words: 'establish limits on the number of universal antlerless deer licenses that hunters could use for each deer management unit in the Upper Peninsula and each county in the Lower Peninsula.' The Order's table is literally keyed two ways — the UP column headed 'Deer Management Unit', the LP column headed 'County'. Fifteen Lower Peninsula DMUs (161, 162, 261, 262, 311, 312, 332, 341, 354, 359, 361, 452, 486, 487, 499) are not coterminous with counties, so a county-keyed limit CANNOT be resolved by DMU lookup. Michigan's Lower Peninsula cannot be answered until county geography exists, with its own licence reviewed to the same standard as any unit layer.
servingDecision.askedOfAuthority: The conformed text of WCO Amendment No. 6 of 2026 as adopted, and its effective date.

discovery.whyThisStateIsTheMostCompleteSoFar: Utah publishes geometry AND the hunt join in one place: layer 0 holds 686 named hunt boundaries, and table 1 (NRDWRGIS.%HUNT_INFO_MOBILE) holds 3,037 rows keyed BOUNDARY_NAME / BOUNDARYID / HUNT_NUMBER / SEASON. So hunt number → boundary → season is resolvable from the authority alone, which is the shape Hunt needs and is rarer than the geometry.
discovery.speciesSpecificGeography: Utah does NOT discriminate species on the boundary layer. Its BTYPE field is null or empty for almost every row — only "CWMU" is populated — so which species and class a boundary serves comes from the HUNT_NUMBER in the join table (for example DB1348), not from the polygon. Anything grouping Utah's geography by a layer attribute would find nothing.
discovery.seasonsAreNotAllPublished: Some SEASON values are not dates: "Contact CWMU Operator for 2026 season dates". Cooperative Wildlife Management Unit seasons are deferred to a private operator, so those hunts are a genuine UNKNOWN even with the join in hand and must never be rendered as a season.
discovery.writtenDescriptionsExist: Each boundary carries a written metes-and-bounds Description. Maine's precedent here is that where a written description accompanies a polygon the description may control; Utah states no precedence either way, and it has not been established.

geography.definedBy: Oregon Administrative Rules chapter 635, Division 080 "WILDLIFE UNITS" — one rule per unit, 635-080-0010 (Saddle Mountain) through 635-080-0077 (Fort Rock). OAR 635-080-0000: for the purpose of managing Oregon's wildlife the State has been divided into separate described areas called wildlife units. The boundary definition is TEXTUAL; the GIS is a depiction of it, and ODFW's own licence note says so by pointing at the OAR division.
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: The layer returns 69 features. 67 are managed units (REGION EAST 47, WEST 20); TWO are REGION='NOT MANAGED' — UNIT_NUM 0 'WARM SPRING INDIAN RESERVATION' and UNIT_NUM 1 'CRATER LAKE NP'. Counting 69 would overstate Oregon's unit system by two AND would draw a reservation and a national park as huntable management units. Corroborated independently: unit numbers run 10–77 with 13 absent, which is exactly 67, and matches the OAR division's per-unit rule numbering.

"Boundaries may not be altered without permission" forbids changing the geometry; it says nothing about drawing it, querying it or redistributing it unchanged. So UNRESOLVED rather than RESTRICTED — classifying an alteration clause as a use refusal would be the over-strict error §8 treats as equally false. It DOES bear on §41B's simplification: a zoom-generalised copy is arguably an altered boundary, and that question is unresolved and load-bearing for how Oregon could ever be drawn.

temporalBreak.finding: Eastern Oregon DEER changed management geography in 2026. The official artifact's "What's new for 2026" (p. 13): a shift from Wildlife Management Units to deer hunt areas, with new hunt names and numbers. ODFW's own article (https://myodfw.com/articles/eastern-oregon-deer-hunts, dated 2025-11-21) explains it: from 2026 eastern Oregon deer hunts are organized by Deer Hunt Areas instead of WMUs, built on 22 mule deer herd ranges identified from over 1,400 GPS-collared deer, renamed alphanumerically (NE-01).
temporalBreak.whyItMatters: A 2025 answer keyed to WMUs is WRONG for 2026 eastern Oregon deer, and a 2026 answer is wrong for 2025. This is a change of geographic IDENTITY, not a boundary adjustment, so no amount of reprojection reconciles them.
temporalBreak.howTheYearIsCarried: By SERVICE NAME, not by a field — the more dangerous form, because a schema check for is_active, year_deactivated or an effective date finds nothing and looks clean. No temporal field exists on any layer. 100Series_HuntBoundary_2026, 400Series_, 500Series_, 700Series_, MD_HuntAreas ("2026"), MD_HerdRanges ("2026"). Searching the owning account for 2025 equivalents returned only the 2026 set, so prior years are retired rather than kept: a stored snapshot cannot answer a past year, and a hard-coded 2026 URL will silently answer the WRONG year once ODFW publishes 2027.

speciesGeography.pattern: SEPARATE ANNUAL LAYERS, one per controlled-hunt series — not an attribute on one layer.
speciesGeography.theOneCharacterTrap: Two services differ by a single character. 100Series_HuntBoundary_2026 (singular) holds BUCK deer at layer 7, 162 features. 100Series_HuntBoundaries_2026 (plural) holds ANTLERLESS deer at layer 1, 72 features. Worse, the portal item pointing at the plural service is TITLED "600Series_HuntBoundaries_2026". Picking by service name alone silently swaps buck and antlerless geography — the same class of hazard as Nevada's.
speciesGeography.layerIdsAreNotZero: Layer ids are 7, 1, 19, 21, 3. A layer-0 assumption fails on almost all of them.
speciesGeography.classIsInTheData: The buck-deer layer's Animal field separates 'One buck with visible antler' (115), 'One mule deer buck with visible antler' (14), 'One white-tailed deer buck with visible antler' (8), 'One white-tailed deer' (8), 'One deer' (6) — so mule, white-tailed and black-tailed deer and the antlered/antlerless class are all distinguished inside one nominal species, which is §16's sex/age-versus-regulatory-class separation arriving as real data.
speciesGeography.theWMUIsOnlyTheBase: Most big-game seasons are set by controlled-hunt areas DERIVED from WMUs: "Hunt Area Entire Wildlife Management Unit unless indicated with an asterisk(*)", with textual controlled-hunt descriptions appended (pp. 94–103). The hunt-boundary layers carry UnitType = full unit (140), subunit (17), multiunit (5) and a HuntDesc field holding the authority's prose. So a coordinate resolves to a WMU, and the applicable hunt area is a full, partial or multi-WMU composite of it, per species and per year.
speciesGeography.gameBirds: No ODFW-owned GIS for waterfowl zones or upland regions was located from any _ODFW or ODFW_AGO account.

CONDITIONS, NOT A REFUSAL — and I am recording a classification I do not share. The discovery pass classified this RESTRICTED. Read against its own words it is not: there is no prohibition on use, reproduction or redistribution anywhere in it. What it states is attribution ("should be clearly cited in any product derived from this Data"), a describe-your-changes condition, an indemnity and a warranty disclaimer. Both of the first two PRESUPPOSE that derived products are permissible — you cannot be required to cite and to describe modifications in a product you may not make. That is materially stronger than Oregon, which restricts alteration outright. But conditions are not a grant either, so UNRESOLVED both ways. §8 is explicit that a restriction stricter than the source is as false as a looser one, and RESTRICTED here would be the strict error: it would park a state whose publisher anticipates derived products.

WHERE IT WAS FOUND MATTERS: the portal ITEM's licenseInfo, not the service. Service-level copyrightText on both PGC_Boundaries and PGC_Hunting_Boundaries is an EMPTY STRING — the New Mexico and Nevada pattern, where reading the service alone returns nothing and looks like silence. The same statement was independently read from four further PGC items (PGC Hunting Boundaries, DMAP Units, CWD, State Game Lands), so it is the account's standard text rather than one layer's.

conflict.finding:
TWO OF THE AUTHORITY'S OWN HOSTS DISAGREE, on two separate layers. Pennsylvania publishes from ArcGIS Online org k8yxvICm95iIFicb (account PAGameCommissionGIS) AND from its own on-premise server pgcmaps.pa.gov, and the two do not match:

Both hosts are the Game Commission's. Neither is obviously stale.
conflict.whyItIsNotResolvedHere: Picking the larger count, the smaller count, or the newer modified date would each be an invention. §8 provides CONFLICT as a state precisely so that this is reportable without being decided, and the elk layer is the one that matters most: elk licences are allocated by zone, so answering 11 where the law uses 14 would send hunters to the wrong zone with a valid-looking answer.
conflict.whatWouldResolveIt: 58 Pa. Code § 139.18 defines the elk zones textually. Reading that section decides the elk conflict from the instrument rather than from either GIS copy. The hours bands resolve the same way, against Appendix G's own meridian figure.

geography.term: COUNTY — Missouri publishes no statewide hunting-unit grid
geography.definedBy: The Wildlife Code of Missouri, Title 3 (Department of Conservation), Division 10 (Conservation Commission), Chapter 7, published by the Missouri Secretary of State. The Code sets deer and turkey regulations BY COUNTY; 115 county polygons are the operative geography, and waterfowl uses its own zones.
geography.theAbsenceIsTheFinding: Missouri does not have a WMU/GMU/unit system, and looking for one is how a state gets recorded as having no geography when it has four. §9 warns against hard-coding one jurisdiction's terminology into a universal model, and Missouri is the case that bites: a resolver that requires a unit layer finds nothing here, while a resolver that accepts the authority's own geography finds counties, deer/turkey county rules and waterfowl zones. Counties are a published Census-and-state geography, so the usual objection — no official polygons — does not apply. What is missing is not geography; it is the zone service, below.

reachability.finding: MDC's own hunting-zone service, gisblue.mdc.mo.gov/arcgis/rest/services/Boundaries/Hunting_Zones/MapServer, does not complete a connection at all — HTTP 0, no response, not a 4xx or 5xx. That service is the one holding Missouri's waterfowl and other published zone geography, so the zones cannot be read even though the county half of the geography can.

evidence.positiveControlSameSweep: services1.arcgis.com/BEFhRGD6ppzvv08z .../Missouri_Counties/FeatureServer/0 returned 200 with 115 features, so the sweep's own fetching worked.

reachability.whyNotWorkedAround: There is no workaround that stays inside §8. A county layer is not a waterfowl zone, and substituting one for the other would answer a zone question with a geography the rule does not use. Nor is a third-party copy acceptable: §44 requires the authority's own service.
reachability.whatWouldUnblockIt: The host responding. It is MDC's own server on MDC's own domain, so this is theirs to fix, and asking is the owner's under the no-contact constraint.
reachability.notTheSameAsLicenceBlocked: Missouri's terms were partly readable and are recorded below. This is a transport failure on one service, not a refusal — the two are undone by completely different actions.

threeInstrumentsThatMustNotBeMerged.statedAs: You may not reproduce this site's text, images, or videos without the Department’s written permission.
threeInstrumentsThatMustNotBeMerged.readsOn: SITE CONTENT — text, images, videos. An express prohibition, and the only express prohibition Missouri states. It does not name data, datasets, geometry or GIS services, and reading it onto them would be the merge this field exists to prevent: it would block Missouri on a sentence about photographs.

threeInstrumentsThatMustNotBeMerged.statedAs: Although all data in this data set have been compiled by the Missouri Department of Agriculture, no warranty, expressed or implied, is made by the department as to the accuracy of the data…
threeInstrumentsThatMustNotBeMerged.readsOn: A WARRANTY DISCLAIMER, and from a different department (Agriculture, not Conservation). It grants nothing and refuses nothing.
An ATTRIBUTION string, complete and verbatim. Not terms at all.

termsReadElsewhere.conclusion: So Missouri has one express prohibition that is about its website, one foreign-department warranty disclaimer, and one attribution string. No instrument states reuse terms for the hunting geography. Classifying the state RESTRICTED on the strength of the website sentence would be the strict error §8 forbids; classifying it permitted would be the loose one. The transport failure is what actually blocks it today.

legalHours.finding: PER SPECIES, and one species states none. There is no single statewide hours rule. From the Wildlife Code, 3 CSR 10-7: deer 10-7.431(4), elk 10-7.700(3) and black bear 10-7.900(4) are each "from one-half (1/2) hour before sunrise until one-half (1/2) hour after sunset". Spring turkey 10-7.455(1)(A)1 runs to 1:00 p.m. CDT on PUBLIC land and to sunset on PRIVATE land. Migratory birds 10-7.440 — doves, rails, woodcock, snipe, ducks, coots and geese — close AT sunset. Rabbits 10-7.420(1) run BETWEEN sunrise and sunset. Squirrels 10-7.425 state a season and limits and NO HOURS AT ALL.
threeThingsThatBreakASingleModel: The big-game window is asymmetric (half an hour before sunrise, half an hour AFTER sunset) while migratory birds close AT sunset. One offset pair cannot be both, and using the big-game pair for ducks would authorise shooting after legal light.
Spring turkey needs a PUBLIC-versus-PRIVATE LAND discriminator before its window can be stated, and its 1:00 p.m. cutoff is written in CDT — a named civil clock, not a solar term.

Squirrels state no hours. §8: that is an unresolved evidentiary gap, not a default. Filling it with the big-game rule would invent a restriction the Code does not impose, and filling it with sunrise-to-sunset would invent a different one.
legalHours.whyNoStateLevelHoursRecordWasAdded: The hours registry holds ONE record per state with one basis. Missouri does not have one basis, so any entry there would be a rounding of the source into the nearest existing field — exactly what §41A forbids. The registry's per-state shape is the limitation, and naming it here is the honest move; expanding it to per-species is real work and is not done by writing a wrong record now.

So even if consent to redistribute were granted, this layer could not answer "which unit am I in" on ADF&G's own terms.
theTermsAlsoForbidTheUseHuntMakes.whyItIsRecordedSeparatelyFromTheLicence: Because the two are undone by different things. Consent would answer the redistribution clause and leave this one standing. theTermsAlsoForbidTheUseHuntMakes.notTheSameAsTheUsualCaveat: §41 already requires that consumer GPS is never presented as a legal survey, and every authority disclaims accuracy. lawVersusGis.finding: THE MOST DANGEROUS FINDING OF THE UNITED STATES SWEEP. KDFWR's own deer-zone layer assigns 46 of Kentucky's 120 counties to a different zone than the law in force. Both publications partition all 120 counties and their county universes are identical, so this is not a coverage artefact — it is a substantive disagreement about zone membership. Adair 1→2, Bath 2→3, Jackson 3→4, Knox 4→3, Pike 3→4, Whitley 4→3, Pulaski 3→4, Madison 2→3, among others.

lawVersusGis.howTheStaleSideWasProven: Not asserted — measured. CURRENTZONE is byte-identical to the same layer's own DZ200708 column across all 120 features: `where=CURRENTZONE<>DZ200708&returnCountOnly=true` returns 0, against a positive control of `where=CURRENTZONE>0` returning 120 on the same layer by the same method. The column aliased "Current Years Deer Zone" is the 2007-08 season, about 19 years stale. The alternatives were ruled out rather than assumed: it matches neither the proposed successor 301 KAR 2:172REG (also 68/24/13/15) nor the immediately prior edition eff. 6-18-2025 (51/35/12/22), so it is neither ahead of the law nor one edition behind — it matches no edition reachable. A third publication breaks the tie: the 2026-27 guide's bag limits match the in-force KAR exactly, and its zone-map legend includes a "Zone change" category, which a layer frozen at 2007-08 cannot express.
lawVersusGis.everySurfaceSignalSaidCurrent: Right publisher, "Annual" in the title, the column aliased "Current Years Deer Zone", lastEditDate and dataLastEditDate 2026-07-10, portal modified 2026-07-10, 120 clean county polygons, exactly four zone values. And the licence is CC0, so no licence check would have stopped it. A clear licence over stale data is more dangerous than a refusal, because a refusal stops you.
lawVersusGis.doNotServe: Do NOT serve CURRENTZONE. Ingesting it would have shipped a plausible, official-looking, KDFWR-published deer-zone map that misstates the zone — and therefore the antlerless bag limit — for 38% of Kentucky. The layer's dated DZ* columns remain legitimate as historical evidence, labelled by their own year.
lawVersusGis.servablePathFromTheLaw: Kentucky IS servable, from the law rather than from the layer: join 301 KAR 2:172's county enumeration to Ky_County_Polygons_WM (CC0). The join matches 120 of 120 counties with zero unmatched names in either direction. Two normalisations are required and neither is a judgement call — they are typographical errors in the regulation itself: it spells "McClean" for McLean and "Elliot" for Elliott.

geography.definedBy: Rule 68A-13.0001, F.A.C., "Definitions", effective 7/1/2026. Subsection (1)(a)–(l) defines TWELVE DMUs — A1, A2, A3, B1, C1, C2, C3, C4, C5, C6, D1, D2 — each as "That portion of Zone [X] located …"; subsection (2)(a)–(d) defines FOUR Zones by county, with many counties split by road or water descriptions.
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: For the DMU layer they AGREE, and that is worth recording because it is the only clean 1:1 layer found in the United States: 12 features, 12 distinct DMU values, 12 codified units, each DMU in exactly one feature, no status field, no region field, no closures, nothing mixed in. The WMA layer is the opposite — 284 features, 160 distinct NAME, 154 among the four hunting-area types, so it overstates by 124. Fifteen features are not hunting-area types at all (2 Air Force Base, 1 Air Force Range, 1 Preserve, 11 Public Use Area) and 121 features carry a UNIT value, meaning one named area is split across several polygons. TYPE_SHORT is not a usable key: "WMA" maps to BOTH "Wildlife Management Area" and "Waterfowl Management Area".
geography.theLayerStopsShortOfTheLaw: The DMU layer's southern limit is ymin 24.8814°N, and Rule 68A-13.0001(2)(a) places the whole of Monroe County — the Florida Keys — in Zone A. Point queries: Key Largo (25.10, -80.44) returns A1/Zone A; Marathon (24.71, -81.09) returns ZERO features; Big Pine Key (24.68, -81.35) returns ZERO. Both misses persisted with tolerance — Big Pine at 10 km and Marathon at 30 km — so this is a layer that stops, not a point that fell in water between islands. FWC's OTHER hunting layer contradicts that limit: the WMA service contains "Florida Keys Wildlife and Environmental Area" with ymin 24.5770°N, about 34 km further south. §8 in both directions: a Keys point below 24.8814°N must not be given an invented DMU, must NOT be reported closed or zoneless when the rule text plainly places it in Zone A, and the mainland must not be discarded because the lower Keys are unresolvable.

PERMITTED WITH REAL CONDITIONS, and the grant is in a THIRD instrument the second one incorporates by reference. The portal item says "Users are encouraged to read and fully comprehend the metadata record prior to using these data" — and the FGDC metadata record is where the reuse position actually is. Verbatim from it: “This data set is in the public domain, and the recipient may not assert any proprietary rights thereto nor represent it to anyone as other than a Florida Fish and Wildlife Conservation Commission produced data set. These data are unrestricted. Where possible, always acquire this dataset directly from FWC as other sources may have altered the original data. FWRI-DC Available without restriction. FOUR CONDITIONS THAT ARE OBLIGATIONS, not caveats to drop: acknowledge FWC as the data source in any product developed from the data; do not assert proprietary rights; do not represent it as other than FWC-produced; and DISTRIBUTE THE METADATA WITH THE DATA SET. The last is the one a normal implementation silently breaks.

Service-level copyrightText is NOT empty here, breaking the usual pattern — but it is an attribution string and states no terms, so it is not the instrument either. The agency's own terms page does not exist: four candidate URLs 404 or return an empty Hub shell, and an enumeration of FWC's ten Hub pages lists no terms page.

separateInstrumentNotMerged.artifact: the annual regulations brochure at eregulations.com
separateInstrumentNotMerged.finding: Hosted by a COMMERCIAL PUBLISHER, not FWC, and the FWC GIS terms say nothing about it. Its reuse position is UNKNOWN and was not established. This blocks nothing: the underlying rules are in the Florida Administrative Code on flrules.org and can be encoded as structured facts in North Ground's own words with the rule cited, which is exactly what §8's "the law's answer, not a copy of the law's prose" provides for.

lawVersusGis.finding: FWC's deer geography stops 34 km north of FWC's own southernmost hunting area, and both stop north of where the rule reaches.
lawVersusGis.lawSays: Rule 68A-13.0001(2)(a) places all of Monroe County in Zone A, and every DMU is a portion of a Zone.
lawVersusGis.gisSays: DMU layer southern limit 24.8814°N; WMA layer southern limit 24.5770°N (Florida Keys WEA).
lawVersusGis.howTheStaleSideWasProven: Queried extents in EPSG:4326 with returnExtentOnly, plus three point queries and two tolerance retries at 10 km and 30 km. No FWC statement explaining the exclusion was found.
lawVersusGis.doNotServe: The mainland and upper Keys ARE servable and must not be discarded. Below 24.8814°N do not give a point a DMU, and do not report it as no-zone or closed — it is an unresolved point inside a zone the law names. Florida's DMU layer is otherwise the only exact 1:1 match with a codified unit list found in the United States.
lawVersusGis.servablePathFromTheLaw: None for the lower Keys as geometry: Rule 68A-13.0001(2)(a) names Monroe County in full, so the zone MEMBERSHIP is known from the text even where the polygon stops — which is enough to say a Keys point is in Zone A, and not enough to say which DMU within it.

geography.term: Zone, per species — Arkansas has no single statewide unit system and the zone sets do not nest
geography.definedBy: The AGFC Code of Regulations. Chapter 02.00 "Zone Regulations" was read directly rather than inferred from its title, and it does NOT contain the deer, bear or turkey zone boundaries — those sit in the Code Addendum chapters with the zone maps published in the annual guidebook.
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: Deer 20 features = 20 distinct labels = 20 guidebook zones: MATCH. Bear 8 = 8: MATCH, at LAYER ID 4, not 0. Alligator 5 at layer 3. CWD 1 at layer 5. But WMA fires the trap twice: WMABoundaries layer 13 returns 139 features for 138 distinct names, and AGFC_Wildlife_Management_Areas_WV returns 192 features for the same 138 — the extra 54 are OWNERSHIP PARCELS inside WMAs, not units. Turkey (5 units) and elk (4 units) have NO published GIS at all, and Elk_Range is not a substitute: its own serviceDescription reads "Elk range as provided by Mr. Watt at UAM Monticello" — a third-party range polygon, not a regulatory boundary.

licence.statedAs: This feature layer was produced by AGFC GIS staff to visualize general location(s) of subject property. Unless otherwise stated, features depicted herein do not represent legal or survey boundaries and are intended for reference purposes only.
licence.note:
THE LICENCE FIELD IS NOT WHERE THE RESTRICTION IS, and this is the state that proves reading it alone produces a false green light. `licenseInfo` — recorded above as `statedAs` — is a boundary-accuracy disclaimer and would block NOTHING on its own. The express limitation of permitted use is in the portal item's `description`: see `termsInTheDescriptionField`. Service-level and layer-level copyrightText are the empty string on every AGFC hunting layer.

The agency's /acceptable-use/ page grants no data reuse and prohibits only website framing ("You may not capture Arkansas.gov pages within frames or present Arkansas.gov content as your own"). The one WMA layer lacking the restriction sentence (AGFC_Wildlife_Management_Areas_WV) states nothing on any of the three instruments, and silence is not a grant. So nothing AGFC publishes grants reuse.

termsInTheDescriptionField.statedAs: This feature layer is intended for educational purposes only and is not for use beyond AGFC's Generation Conservation Summit. Data in this feature layer is accurate as of 2025-08-11. Any changes to AGFC's deer zones after 2025-08-11 will not be reflected in this feature layer.
termsInTheDescriptionField.whyItMatters: "is not for use beyond AGFC's Generation Conservation Summit" limits permitted use to ONE INTERNAL AGFC EVENT. For a public product that is a refusal — not an attribution condition, not an indemnity, not an accuracy caveat. The same sentence appears on the bear, alligator, CWD and WMA items with the species word swapped, so it is the account's standard text rather than one layer's slip.
termsInTheDescriptionField.whatTheLicenceFieldSaidInstead: An accuracy disclaimer: features "do not represent legal or survey boundaries and are intended for reference purposes only". Recording that as the terms would have cleared Arkansas.

findings.note: The restriction is a scope limit on those PUBLISHED ARTEFACTS, not a copyright claim over the underlying facts. The zone identities — 20 deer zones, 8 bear zones, 5 turkey zones — are facts stated in the Code and the guidebook and may be encoded in North Ground's own words under §8. What cannot be used is AGFC's geometry.

geography.term: Indiana has NO single named hunting-unit system: County for deer bag limits, Deer Reduction Zone, and Waterfowl Hunting Zone are three different geographies with three different legal terms
geography.definedBy: the portal item's own metes-and-bounds description ("North: That part of Indiana north of a line extending east from the Illinois border along State Road 18 to U.S. 31…")
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: Counties 92 = 92: match. Waterfowl zones 3 = 3: match. But Deer Reduction Zones return 34 features for only 18 distinct NAMED zones — 15 features carry a BLANK `Area` (verified: `where=Area='  '&returnCountOnly=true` returns 15) — so 34 overstates by about 1.9x, and the fields `unitname` and `SymbolID` are entirely blank and unusable as keys. The service name "Traditional & Corridors" explains it: one named zone carries a traditional polygon plus corridor polygons. Public hunting properties: 190 features, 120 distinct properties, at LAYER ID 1 — layer 0 does not exist on that service.

licence.statedAs: DATA DISCLAIMER: This item, including its underlying data, is restricted for use by the Indiana Department of Natural Resources (IDNR) Division of Fish & Wildlife and approved partners only.
licence.attribution: Indiana Department of Natural Resources, Division of Fish & Wildlife
licence.note:
AN EXPRESS RESTRICTION ON WHO MAY USE THE DATA, and it lands on the one layer that matters. North Ground is not an "approved partner". It is not cured by the item being access:public or by the word "Public" in its title. Indiana's ONLY genuine regulatory-zone vector layer — 3 features, 3 units, clean, current — is the one we may not use.

ONE AGENCY, TWO DIFFERENT INSTRUMENTS. The county bag-limit, Deer Reduction Zone, CWD and deer-density items carry a DIFFERENT licenseInfo that is warranty and liability language only, with no refusal. So Indiana cannot be classified from one item; the restriction must be read per dataset.

Service-level copyrightText is an empty string on all thirteen Indiana services checked, with a positive control (USGS basemap) confirming the reader surfaces real copyrightText when present — so the emptiness is Indiana's, not the method's. Reading only the service would have concluded everything was free to use.

This is NOT a §8 reproduction-licence question that can be routed around by re-expressing the rule in our own words: the restriction is on USING THE DATA, and the data here is geometry, not prose. The zone DEFINITIONS are published as metes-and-bounds text in the item description and could in principle be encoded independently — that route is untested and would need its own authorization.

lawVersusGis.finding: A layer titled "Active CWD Indiana Counties upd. 05/2026" and described as "all Indiana counties that are active CWD zones as of 05/2026" CONTAINS ALL 92 COUNTIES — i.e. it asserts the entire state is an active CWD zone.
lawVersusGis.lawSays: The same author's companion item, "CWD Positive Townships upd. 05/2026", holds 5 positive townships.
lawVersusGis.gisSays: 92 of 92 counties, at layer 105 of CWD_CountyZones_2024_ExportFeatures.

speciesHeatCandidate.finding: 9,318 one-square-mile cells of estimated deer density — the best US deer-abundance evidence found so far, at LAYER ID 132. Relevant to §41B rather than to the map lane, and subject to the same instrument question: it carries Indiana's conditions-only licenseInfo, not the waterfowl refusal.
speciesHeatCandidate.doNotActOnItYet: §41B requires a declared resolution, evidence class, methodology and confidence before any surface is drawn. None of that is established here.

geography.term: Deer Season Zone (A–E), Turkey Season Zone (1–3), dove North/South Zone, CWD Management Zone with High-Risk and Buffer Zones, Mobile-Tensaw Delta Waterfowl Management Zone, five Alligator Management Areas
geography.definedBy: Ala. Admin. Code r. 220-2-.01 and r. 220-2-.77, Agency 220 Chapter 220-2 "Game And Fish Division". Deer Zones A–E are defined ONLY as narrative metes-and-bounds along highways, rivers, bypasses and county lines — Zone A's description alone runs about 2,300 characters — and Zones B–E are partly defined by EXCLUSION ("Excludes Zones C, D, and E").
geography.theAbsenceIsTheFinding:
THE SPECIES-DETERMINATIVE GEOGRAPHY IS NOT PUBLISHED AS VECTOR DATA BY ANYONE. ADCNR's own ArcGIS Server has 46 services and not one is a zone layer — confirmed from the authoritative directory listing and by probing DeerZones, HuntingZones, TurkeyZones, Zones and CWD, each of which returns HTTP 200 carrying {"error":{"code":404,"message":"Service not found"}}. A point therefore CANNOT be resolved to an Alabama deer zone. Deriving those lines ourselves from highway centrelines, river courses and bypass alignments would be North Ground inventing a regulatory boundary, which §41A forbids outright. Deer — Alabama's most-hunted species — is unserviceable at point resolution, and that is a genuine evidentiary gap, not an implementation limitation.

Turkey and dove are different: those zones are COUNTY LISTS (turkey Zone 1 = 44 counties, Zone 2 = 9, Zone 3 = 6; dove South = 9 named counties, North = all others), and ADCNR publishes 67 county polygons. One county is split by text ("Cullman (except north of Lewis Smith Lake and north of Cullman County Road 437 and west of I-65)"), so turkey is resolvable for 66 counties and unresolved inside Cullman.
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: The 42-feature "WildlifeManagementAreas" layer is not 42 WMAs. By name suffix it holds 29 WMA, 4 Tract, 3 Management Area, 2 NATIONAL WILDLIFE REFUGE (federal: Cahaba River, Key Cave), 2 Refuge and 2 Community Hunting Area — and the layer carries NO class or status field, so class is recoverable only by parsing the name string. Three features are absent from r. 220-2-.22 entirely (Dutch Bend, Jacinto Port and Tom Roush Tracts), and the layer calls "Grand Bay Savanna" a Wildlife Management Area where the rule establishes it as a Community Hunting Area. The SOA layer's 15 exceeds the rule's 13.
geography.theLegalBoundaryIsElsewhere: r. 220-2-.22(1) fixes it expressly: "The boundary lines of these areas and refuges shall be as they are described on the maps attached in Chapter 220-2-A Appendix A." The GIS layer is therefore not the legal boundary instrument even for the areas it does cover.

licenceAbsent.finding: No instrument reachable states any reuse, redistribution, attribution or derived-product term for Alabama's hunting geography — and none states a prohibition either. Service-level copyrightText is the empty string at both MapServer and layer level on all five hunting-relevant services, and serviceDescription and description are empty too. There is NO ARCGIS PORTAL ITEM AT ALL, so the instrument that carried the terms in Kentucky, Arkansas, Indiana, Pennsylvania and New Jersey does not exist here.
whereLooked: service copyrightText at MapServer and layer level, five services
ArcGIS portal item licenseInfo — no portal item exists
licenceAbsent.controlForTheAbsence: The same reader surfaces real copyrightText elsewhere in the same sweep (Florida's is a non-empty attribution string, Washington's lines item carries a full caveat), so the emptiness is Alabama's and not the method's.
licenceAbsent.whatWouldUnblockIt: ADCNR stating terms for its GIS, which is the owner's to ask.
licenceAbsent.whyItsOwnStateAndNotReachability: Every service answered 200. Nothing is unreachable; nothing is stated.

conflict.finding: Two ADCNR publications disagree about the extent of the CWD Management Zone. The codified rule, r. 220-2-.01(1)(f)6 effective 5 June 2026, read in both the HTML render and independently in the rule PDF: "The CWD Management Zone (CMZ) includes all of Lauderdale, Colbert, and Franklin Counties" — THREE whole counties. The agency's own outdooralabama.com page states a different extent.
conflict.whyItIsNotResolvedHere: The codified rule is the instrument and would normally govern, but the CMZ contains a High-Risk Zone and a Buffer Zone whose boundaries are also narrative, and no vector geometry exists for any of them — so there is nothing to serve either way. Recording the disagreement is the whole available action.
conflict.whatWouldResolveIt: ADCNR reconciling its web page with r. 220-2-.01(1)(f)6, or publishing the CMZ as geometry.

legalHours.finding: A THIRD KIND OF HOURS RULE, and the inverse of Washington and Pennsylvania. Not a table dressed as a formula — a term with NO FORMULA AT ALL. Ala. Admin. Code r. 220-2-.05, "Legal Hunting Hours For Game Birds": "Legal hunting hours for game birds during the open season shall be daylight hours only, except as otherwise provided by law or regulation." "Daylight hours" is UNDEFINED in the rule. North Ground's astronomy cannot reproduce it because there is no numeric rule to reproduce, and choosing an offset would be inventing the law. Alabama then layers computable solar offsets and fixed civil clock times onto specific species and geographies.
legalHours.contrastWithKentucky: Kentucky states the same phrase and DEFINES it: KRS 150.010(8), "'Daylight hours' means the period from one-half (1/2) hour before sunrise to one-half (1/2) hour after sunset." So the identical words are certifiable in one state and not in the other, and the difference is a statutory definition. Carrying Kentucky's definition into Alabama would be the exact error §8 forbids.

For deer, 17 Ill. Adm. Code 650.10(b): "Permit quotas shall be set by the Department of Natural Resources on a county or special hunt area basis."

Iowa Code ch. 481A and ch. 483A were checked and contain NO statutory hunting-hours provision, with a positive control run for that absence.
geography.theFeatureCountIsNotTheUnitCount: 86 features, and neither 86 nor the 74 distinct attribute combinations is a unit count. 81 features form a single statewide tessellation — proven by area arithmetic, not by assumption: sum(Shape__Area) where NR_Deer IS NOT NULL is 145,581 km² against Iowa's ~145,746 km², n=81. The other 5 are an OVERLAY, not units: they are the only rows where every species field is NULL, they carry the field aliased "Closed Canada Goose Area", and their envelopes are five small areas totalling about 109 km² near Oelwein, Bellevue, Lake Panorama, Creston and Winterset. Counting them as zones is exactly the trap.

Service-level copyrightText "" on the FeatureServer root and "" with empty description on layers 1, 2 and 3; portal item 4a015ae7b9cd4f73a0f49a974c1682d7 licenseInfo "" and accessInformation ""; item a39cc7a1b18346a3a42ccf263dec7ac0 licenseInfo null. conflict.finding: Resident Fall Turkey Zone 9 is quota'd and mapped but never defined in text. IAC 571—98.2(3) sets fall resident quotas for SIX zones ("a. Zone 4: 1,500. b. Zone 5: 650. c. Zone 6: 1,400. d. Zone 7: 250. e. Zone 8: 200. f. Zone 9: 200."), while IAC 571—98.10 "Zones open to hunting" defines only FIVE zones textually — 4, 5, 6, 7 and 8, by highways. The GIS layer carries six distinct values, 4 to 9, with 12 polygons at Zone 9, and the booklet's printed map shows a 9. So Zone 9 exists in three of the authority's publications and in none of its boundary definitions.
conflict.whyItIsNotResolvedHere: A quota and a map label are not a boundary definition. Serving Zone 9's polygons would assert a boundary the rule that opens the zone does not state; refusing all six would discard five zones that ARE defined, which §8 forbids.
conflict.whatWouldResolveIt: IAC 571—98.10 being amended to define Zone 9, or the incorporated-by-reference map being identified for it.

findings.note: A PREDICTION THAT WAS WRONG, recorded because it changes the verdict. I expected Iowa to be county-only geography with no zone service, and the atlas layer to hold about 99 county polygons. Both were wrong in the same direction: Iowa publishes a genuine multi-species zone layer tiling into 81 units. Iowa is MORE servable than expected, not less, and the only thing standing in the way is that its terms are unstated.

silenceIsNotRefusal: Two different states of the world are both recorded as blocked, and they are undone differently. SILENCE (UNRESOLVED) means no grant is stated either way: the publisher may simply never have been asked, so a person must ask it. A REFUSAL (RESTRICTED, or redistribution PROHIBITED) means the publisher has answered, and the answer is no: reading its terms more carefully will not change them, and only a written exception from it would. Reporting the two identically would make a refusal look like an errand.
reachabilityIsNotLicence: A source that cannot be reached SECURELY is blocked for a different reason than one whose terms refuse us, and the two must not be merged. Arizona is the first: its own GIS host has served an expired certificate since 2022, so North Ground has never been able to read its terms at all. Recording that as a licence finding would assert something about terms nobody has read; recording it as 'no source' would be false, because the authority publishes one. It is its own state, and the remedy belongs to the authority rather than to us.
aWarrantyDisclaimerIsNotALicence: Several states answer a licence question with a WARRANTY disclaimer, which is a different legal instrument: it disclaims liability for accuracy and says nothing about reuse. Nevada's whole statement is one. Reading "no warranty" as "no permission" would invent a refusal; reading it as permission would invent a grant. Both are UNRESOLVED, and the note says which kind of silence it is, because a disclaimer means the publisher HAS written terms and they simply do not address use — which is a different ask than a publisher who has written nothing.
threeWaysAFindingCanLackALicence: A finding carries exactly one of: `licence` (terms were read, whatever they say), `reachability` (the service could not be reached securely, so its terms could not be read either — Arizona), or `licenceAbsent` (the service is fine and the publisher has stated nothing — Utah). They are not interchangeable because the next action differs: read the terms, ask the authority to fix its certificate, or ask the authority to state terms at all.
